findings.title: Bed filter on Waterings page is lost on reload/shared link (query param mismatch bed vs bed_id)
findings.steps: Open /waterings (or via 'Watering history' link, which uses ?bed=1). Choose 'Shade corner' in the Bed filter. URL becomes /waterings?bed_id=2. Reload the page or open that URL.
findings.expected: Filter stays on Shade corner, showing only its waterings.
findings.actual: Page reads route.query.bed but writes bed_id, so after reload the filter resets to 'All beds' and every watering is listed.
findings.evidence: URL after selecting was http://localhost:3792/waterings?bed_id=2; after reload select value was '' and the list showed waterings from all beds.

findings.title: Water now on a second bed re-enables the first bed's button; double watering recorded and notices lost
findings.steps: With a slow network (POST /api/waterings delayed 2.5 s), click 'Water now' on North bed, then 'Water now' on Shade corner, then 'Water now' on North bed again.
findings.expected: North bed's button stays disabled until its request finishes; one watering per click intent; each bed shows its own result.
findings.actual: wateringBedId is overwritten by the second bed, so North bed's button is re-enabled while its request is in flight and a second click creates a duplicate. The first request to finish sets wateringBedId to null and re-enables everything. Only one success notice is kept (Shade corner's was lost).
findings.evidence: North bed waterings count went 5 -> 7. northDisabledWhilePending=false. Only alert visible: 'Watered North bed.'

findings.title: Watering requests have no timeout; Water now spins forever when the server does not answer
findings.where: /beds Water now and Save watering; /waterings Delete; dashboard and waterings GETs
findings.steps: Make POST /api/waterings hang (no response). Click 'Water now' on a bed and wait more than 10 s.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error and the button is enabled again.
findings.actual: After 14 s the button still said 'Watering…' and was disabled. No timeout is set in useApiClient or useApiFetch.
findings.evidence: Button text 'Watering… North bed', disabled=true after 14 s.

findings.title: Waterings page and dashboard 'Recent waterings' error states have no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings return 503. Navigate in the app to Waterings, then to Dashboard.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that reloads the data once the server is back.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load waterings.' / 'Could not load recent waterings.' is shown, with no retry control (the dashboard doesn't even destructure refresh for waterings). The user has to reload the whole page.
findings.evidence: Only button on the page was 'Sign out' in both cases.

findings.title: Waterings page hides a failed bed list: the filter silently shows only 'All beds'
findings.steps: Make GET /api/beds fail while opening /waterings through the app.
findings.expected: An error saying the beds could not be loaded, with a retry.
findings.actual: bedsResult.error is ignored. The dropdown just has fewer or no bed options and no message.
findings.evidence: Code: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult`, with no error handling. Rendering falls back to `beds ?? []`.

findings.title: Very large IDs return 500 Internal Server Error from watering endpoints
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error, because the int exceeds SQLite's 64-bit range and raises OverflowError. Neither bed_id nor watering_id has an upper bound.
findings.evidence: HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' for all three requests.

findings.title: When the list refresh fails after Water now, the whole bed list is replaced by an error with no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/beds return 500 and click 'Water now' on a bed.
findings.expected: The watering is confirmed and the existing bed list stays, or a retry is offered.
findings.actual: The watering was saved, but the list area becomes only 'Could not load beds.', with no retry. The success notice and the beds disappear.
findings.evidence: Watering count went 4 -> 5. Main area text after the click: 'All beds\nCould not load beds.'

findings.title: Extreme dates and tiny amounts are accepted and display oddly ('1 Jan 1', '0 L')
findings.steps: Record a past watering dated 0001-01-01 with litres 0.000000001 (through the form or the API).
findings.expected: An unrealistic date or amount is refused with a reason, or the amount is shown correctly.
findings.actual: Accepted with 201. It is listed as '1 Jan 1' and '0 L', and it appears in the dashboard's recent waterings.
findings.evidence: Waterings table row: '1 Jan 1  North bed  0 L'.

findings.title: 'Water now' date uses the server's local date and the future-date check uses the server's today, not the gardener's
findings.steps: Use the browser in a time zone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+10 when the server is UTC), shortly after local midnight. Record a past watering for today (the form's default and max is the browser's today).
findings.actual: The server rejects it with 'Watering date cannot be in the future.' because it compares with date.today() on the server. 'Water now' entries also get watered_on from the server's date, which can differ from the displayed local time.
findings.evidence: Code: not_in_future uses date.today(); watered_on = now.astimezone().date(); the form uses the client's todayIso().

findings.title: No idempotency for creating waterings; retrying after a timeout or lost response creates duplicates
findings.steps: Click Water now. The response is lost after the server commits, so the user sees an error and clicks again.
findings.actual: Each POST inserts a new row. There is no idempotency key or dedupe.
findings.evidence: Code review. Combined with the missing timeout and the refresh issue above, the user is invited to retry.
